title: Utilities propose protections as data centers strain Maryland's power grid
source_used: Patch (Across Maryland, 30 Sep 2026); Baltimore Sun page returned no article text
key_facts: BGE, Pepco and Delmarva Power, which serve more than 1 million Maryland customers, filed a 'large load tariff' with the Maryland Public Service Commission on Tuesday 29 Sep 2026.
BGE says the tariff would require large new customers, including data centers, to pay their fair share of grid costs that all customers rely on.
A PSC hearing on the filing is scheduled for 23 Oct 2026, with further hearings 8 to 11 Dec 2026.
Separately, the same utilities announced on Monday 28 Sep 2026 that they seek approval to pass about $160 million in tax savings to customers after a Maryland Supreme Court ruling in July.
Comptroller Brooke Lierman said the refunded taxes belong to ratepayers.
BGE faced pushback over the summer for proposing an $8 monthly rate increase worth about $156 million.
quote_evidence: BGE said in a release that a large load tariff filing was submitted to the PSC, requiring that "large new customers, including data centers, would pay their fair share toward the grid all customers rely on."
A PSC hearing on the filing is scheduled for Oct. 23, with additional hearings scheduled between Dec. 8 and Dec. 11.
In Maryland, more than 1 million customers are served by BGE, Pepco and Delmarva Power.
why_it_matters_hint: Maryland utilities want data centers to carry their own grid costs so household bills do not rise with them.
notes: Baltimore Sun returned HTTP 200 but only a copyright notice (AMP too). Patch wrote its own report of the filing; used as source. Event is 4 to 5 days old.
